system_overview: This specification models a one-step consensus algorithm with zero degradation under crash faults, based on Algorithm 2 (lines 1-4) from Dobre and Suri's 2006 DSN paper. The protocol allows processes to reach consensus in one communication step when all processes propose the same value, with no performance degradation compared to standard consensus when proposals differ. Only the one-step algorithm is modeled, without the underlying consensus sub-protocol.
actors_and_components: The system consists of N processes, some of which may become faulty (crash). The protocol tolerates up to T faults, with up to F actually occurring (F at most T). The constraint N greater than 3T is required. Faulty processes may contribute messages with arbitrary values before or after crashing. Correct processes follow the protocol faithfully.
state_variables: The system tracks: the number of vote-for-0 messages sent by correct processes, the number of vote-for-1 messages sent by correct processes, the number of vote-for-0 messages attributed to faulty processes, the number of vote-for-1 messages attributed to faulty processes, the count of currently faulty processes, the control location of each process (initial proposal of 0 or 1, sent vote for 0 or 1, decided 0 or 1, deferred to underlying consensus with 0 or 1, or Byzantine/faulty), and the number of vote-for-0 and vote-for-1 messages received by each process.
initial_state: Initially, no messages of any kind have been sent (all message counts are zero). No process is faulty. Each process starts in one of two proposal states, nondeterministically choosing to propose 0 or 1. All received message counts are zero. Two special initial configurations are defined: one where all processes propose 0, and one where all processes propose 1.
actions: The protocol supports the following transitions: (1) A process that is not yet faulty may become faulty if the faulty count is below F. When becoming faulty, it may contribute a message for the opposite value. (2) A process that proposed 0 broadcasts a vote for 0 and moves to the sent-0 state. A process that proposed 1 broadcasts a vote for 1 and moves to the sent-1 state. (3) A process may receive a vote-for-0 or vote-for-1 message (if more have been sent than received, including messages from faulty processes). (4) After sending its vote, once a process has received at least N-T total messages, it decides based on the following rules: (a) if it received at least N-T votes for 0, it decides 0; (b) if it received at least N-T votes for 1, it decides 1; (c) if neither threshold is met and the process originally voted for 0, it defers to underlying consensus with value 0; (d) similarly if it voted for 1, it defers with value 1.
safety_properties: OneStep0: if all processes initially propose 0, then no process ever defers to underlying consensus with value 0, defers with value 1, or decides 1. OneStep1 (liveness form): if all processes initially propose 1, then eventually no process is in a state of having deferred with 0, deferred with 1, or decided 0.
liveness_properties: OneStep1 includes a liveness component: if all processes propose 1, eventually all processes reach a state where none has decided 0 or deferred to underlying consensus.
model_bounds: For model checking: N=4, T=1, F=1. The process set is 1 through N. Control locations include nine distinct states: two initial proposal states, two sent-vote states, two decided states, two deferred-to-underlying states, and one Byzantine/faulty state.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed on receiving, proposing, and deciding actions for all processes, ensuring progress when these actions are continuously enabled. The model uses a message-counting abstraction rather than tracking individual messages. The specification requires N greater than 3T, T at least F, and F at least 0. When a process becomes faulty, it may inject a message for the value opposite to its proposal.
